the cancel button does not mean your the cancel button does not mean your transfer is cancelled immediately i am very disappointed with wise s cancellation process. the interface gives the impression that cancelling a transfer is as simple as clicking cancel. however, cancellation is apparently not immediate. i was informed that it can take up to two working days to process the cancellation. that means the situation is very different from what the cancellation button suggests you may click cancel, but your money can remain tied up for up to two working days while you wait for the cancellation to actually be completed. this is a serious issue when dealing with money. if a customer decides they need to cancel a transfer, they may reasonably expect the cancellation to happen promptly and the funds to become available again. instead, they can be left waiting for days. i believe wise should make this limitation clearly and prominently visible before the customer confirms the cancellation. a simple cancel button without an obvious warning that the process may take up to two working days creates an impression of immediate cancellation that does not match the actual process. financial services should be transparent about when customers will regain access to their money. two working days is not a minor detail it can be financially significant. wise may provide a convenient transfer service, but the cancellation process needs much greater transparency. customers should not have to discover only after clicking cancel that their money may remain unavailable for up to two working days. my advice to anyone using wise before sending a transfer, be aware that cancelling it may not be an immediate process, and your money may remain tied up while the cancellation is being processed.
